x: Four of our young milers, Clements, Chantler, Stimpson and Wood competed in an under 20 mile team race at the Enfield A.C. Open Meeting, and although our scoring men finished 4, 5, 6, we were placed second.
Wood, Herne Hill H. Putting in a fast lap he caught them, and at the bell was leading by a yard or two.
George Chantler (the holder), Dave Martin, Ed Stimpson and Ken Wood were always close together; but in the closing stages Stimpson found a little extra speed to finish nine seconds ahead of Martin.

He was passed by a bunch of runners including Beaumont, Wood, Merryman, Jordan and Bert Mitchell. About 600 yards from the finish Beaumont was leading and over the last stretch he increased his lead by a few yards to beat Jordan (who was making a good effort to catch him) by 2 seconds, followed by W…
Wood, who gained the individual title.
At this point we had Murdoch in the first half-dozen, with Clements, Beaumont and Wood in the early twenties. From here it was obvious we should be placed.

Our two most prominent juniors, Stimpson and Wood, ran magnificently in such company. In conclusion, I must express the thoughts of all: how we missed that diminutive figure, red of face, black of hair, running this year!

Penny was next, followed by Carter, Cohen, Ring, and Wood (who won the Surrey Junior Race the week after) in the first twenty places. Our hopes of repeating our win of last year were now very bright; and we next saw the field coming round Tattenham Corner led by Bert Footer, followed by Belton.
About half-way, Clements managed to open up a gap from Wood and a mile from home had established a lead of two hundred yards, which was never reduced.
Beaumont, Wood and Tobin are all likely to show improved performances next year. We detect plenty of evidence of another winning team in a year or two.
Long Jump: 1 Bull, 18 ft. 9½ ins.; 3 Jones, 17 ft. 11½ in.s Shot: 1 Wood (D.), 34 ft. 4½ ins.; 2 Melchior, 33 ft. 11¼ ins. Discus: 1 Wood (D.), 105 ft.; 2 Melchior, 90 ft. 7 ins.; 4 Powell, 80 ft.
Len Herbert did not find the going to his liking and finished no nearer than 19th closely followed by our Poly member, Jimmy Wood, who had ran steadily throughout to finish 23rd.

A fast start along the embankment to Chelsea Bridge soon strung out the field which was led by Wood of Sheffield United Harriers who had recently performed creditably in the International Cross Country closely followed by Parmenter of Birchfield and Wood of Surrey A.C.
He was in the lead for the first mile with Dunkley of Shaftesbury, but then Wood of Sheffield went past and opened up the field in the course of his record breaking run.

At Chelsea Bridge the leaders made a break and Wood(Sheffield), Mayatt(Aylesford), Gilligan(Pembroke) and Eales(Tipton) opened up a thirty yards lead from seven others (including Pete) by Queens Road Circus.

Wood, a further 50 yards down. After 4½ miles John Moore had established himself in second place, about 200 yards behind Maynard, while Wood and Shippen, still running together, had virtually caught Thompson.

Penny was next, followed by Carter, Cohen, Ring, and Wood (who won the Surrey Junior Race the week after) in the first twenty places. Our hopes of repeating our win of last year were now very bright; and we next saw the field coming round Tattenham Corner led by Bert Footer.
About this time, Bill finished 3rd in the Club Junior 5 miles Championship and scored in a winning Surrey Junior Cross-country team (Wood 1, Herbert 4, Lucas 5, Shepherd 6).
Arthur Bruce had been called in at the last minute after Bert Stroud had gone down with flu and did well to run round in 25:43 but at the front Pulman of TVH ran 23:20 and Wood of Barnet 23:43.
